note: The stage-5 spec for this state, nominated BEFORE anything was built (see docs/IMPORT-A-STATE.md). Six corridors a local cyclist rides on ordinary roads, chosen to cover Oregon's distinct regions rather than to be easy. Read by scripts/test_corridor_severance.mjs. 'maxRatio' is a severance detector, not a distance pin (lesson G2): it catches 'the router went around three counties', not 'this is 8% longer than last month'.

corridors.name: Portland -> Hood River (Columbia Gorge)
corridors.why: The Historic Columbia River Highway State Trail is the signed non-freeway way east through the Gorge. The Mitchell Point tunnel opened in 2024, but ODOT confirms a remaining 0.7-mile bicycle gap west of it; construction of that connection began in December 2025 and is expected through late 2026. Until it opens, I-84 is the only through line and the router must not invent a bicycle-legal trail connection.

corridors.name: Astoria -> Tillamook (north coast, US 101)
corridors.why: The Oregon Coast Bike Route, and the first leg of Adventure Cycling's Pacific Coast route. US 101 is the only continuous corridor; the Coast Range has no parallel road. Tests that the router will use a real highway when a highway is what exists, instead of inventing a hundred-mile logging-road detour.

corridors.name: Eugene -> Corvallis (Willamette Valley)
corridors.why: The densest low-stress grid in the state and the spine of the Willamette Valley Scenic Bikeway. Two university towns 36 miles apart with a lattice of farm roads between them: if this one comes back long, the problem is the router, not the corridor.

corridors.name: Bend -> Sisters (Central Oregon)
corridors.why: High desert east of the Cascades, where the network is sparse and OR 126 / OR 20 carry everything. The Twin Bridges loop out of Bend is one of the most-ridden routes in the state; a rider gets there on ordinary road.

corridors.name: Medford -> Ashland (Rogue Valley)
corridors.why: The Bear Creek Greenway is a continuous separated path linking these two, parallel to I-5. Short, southern, and the one corridor where a fully separated facility should be the obvious answer -- so a freeway or an arterial in the shortest option means the path is severed.

corridors.name: Baker City -> John Day (Eastern Oregon)
corridors.why: Adventure Cycling's TransAmerica Trail runs this, and it is the emptiest quarter of the state: US 26 and OR 7 over Dixie and Tipton passes with nothing either side for fifty miles. Tests the half of Oregon where a severed link has no alternative at all.
